title: Corinne Whitaker
content:
Whitaker has been associated with early online creative culture and has been described as part of a generation of artists who explored the internet as a primary medium for artistic expression.[1] Her work combines artistic practice with philosophical and technological themes, often incorporating elements of identity, abstraction, and digital transformation.

Early life and background

Whitaker is of Nubian descent, an influence that has informed aspects of her artistic identity and thematic exploration.[2] Her work often reflects a synthesis of cultural heritage and digital experimentation, blending traditional artistic concepts with emerging technologies.

Career

Early internet presence

Whitaker established an online presence during the early years of the internet, including activity associated with the domain giraffe.com, which has been cited as an example of early personal web publishing.[3] Her work during this period contributed to the emergence of independent digital creators using the internet as a platform for artistic dissemination.

Digital Giraffe

Whitaker is the founder and chief creative force behind Digital Giraffe, a platform dedicated to experimental digital creativity.[1] Through this platform, she has published visual artwork, poetry, essays, and multimedia projects.

Her blog, digitalgiraffe.blogspot.com, serves as an archive of her ongoing work and reflections on creativity, technology, and artistic philosophy.[1]

Artistic practice

Whitaker’s work spans multiple disciplines, including:

  • Digital painting and visual art
  • Digital sculpture
  • Poetry and prose writing
  • Experimental and AI-assisted music composition

Her artistic approach is often described as interdisciplinary, combining visual, textual, and auditory elements into a unified creative expression.[1] She has referred to aspects of her work as “betaphysical,” a term used to explore the intersection of metaphysics, consciousness, and digital creation.[1]

Philosophy and themes

Whitaker’s work emphasizes the fluidity of artistic identity and the role of technology as both a tool and a medium. Her practice reflects themes such as transformation, perception, and the evolving relationship between humans and digital environments.[1]

She has adopted titles such as “Chief Imagineer” and “Digital Giraffe,” reflecting a self-defined creative identity rooted in imagination and multidimensional expression.[1]

Selected works and platforms

  • Digital Giraffe (creative platform)
  • digitalgiraffe.blogspot.com (blog and archive of works)

Legacy and influence

Whitaker is considered part of a broader movement of early digital creators who used the internet as a platform for independent artistic expression. Her work reflects the evolution of digital art practices from early web publishing to contemporary multimedia experimentation.[3]

title: Alan John Mayer
content:
Alan John Mayer was born in Casablanca, Morocco, into a family with an international background. His father served as a diplomat associated with the United States Department of Defense, which resulted in Mayer spending much of his childhood moving between countries. [2]

Due to these frequent relocations, Mayer attended a variety of schools across different cultural and educational systems. This early exposure to diverse perspectives is often cited as a formative influence on his later interest in human consciousness, identity, and cross-cultural understanding. [2]

Mayer later pursued higher education in the United States. He earned a Bachelor of Arts in Theater and Television Production, reflecting an early interest in storytelling and media. He also obtained an Associate of Arts in Psychology, which contributed to his engagement with themes related to human behavior and cognition. In addition, he received a K–Adult Teaching Credential from the University of California, Irvine, supporting his work in education. [2]

Career

Mayer’s career spans both education and writing, with a focus on integrating psychological insight and philosophical inquiry into narrative forms.

He has worked as an educator, applying his academic training in psychology and communication to teaching across different age groups. His teaching work has often intersected with his interest in personal development and introspective learning approaches. [2]

Since 1991, Mayer has been a licensed practitioner of the Science of Mind philosophy, a spiritual and metaphysical system associated with the broader New Thought movement. His involvement in this tradition has informed both his teaching and his literary work, particularly in areas related to self-awareness, belief systems, and the nature of reality. [2]

Mayer has also studied and taught concepts associated with A Course in Miracles, a spiritual text that emphasizes forgiveness, perception, and inner transformation. These influences are reflected in the philosophical underpinnings of his fiction. [2]

Literary work

Mayer is best known for his contributions to philosophical fiction, a genre that combines narrative storytelling with exploration of abstract and introspective themes.

His most prominent work is the A Boy Alone series, which follows a protagonist navigating complex psychological and existential challenges. The series incorporates allegory and symbolic storytelling to examine ideas such as identity, consciousness, morality, and personal growth. [1]

Bibliography

A Boy Alone series

  • A Boy Alone
  • A Boy Alone: The Grand Tour (2021) [1]

Themes and style

Mayer’s writing is characterized by its integration of narrative fiction with philosophical and psychological exploration.

Recurring themes in his work include:

  • The nature of consciousness and perception
  • Personal transformation and self-discovery
  • Moral introspection and ethical decision-making
  • The relationship between inner belief systems and external reality

His storytelling often employs allegorical structures, where characters and environments function as representations of internal psychological states. Symbolism and introspective dialogue are frequently used to explore abstract concepts in an accessible narrative format. [1]

Reception

Coverage of Mayer’s work has primarily appeared on book distribution platforms and author-managed channels. His writing has been described as philosophical fiction that blends storytelling with spiritual and psychological inquiry. [1]

As of now, independent critical coverage in major literary journals or mainstream media remains limited, and additional secondary sources would be required to establish broader recognition in academic or literary criticism.

Personal philosophy and influences

Mayer’s work reflects a synthesis of influences from:

  • New Thought philosophy
  • Psychology and human development
  • Spiritual teachings such as A Course in Miracles

His approach emphasizes introspection, self-awareness, and the transformative potential of thought and perception, which are recurring elements across both his teaching and writing.

title: Sigma
content:
Opción Sigma (Sigma Option LLC) is a financial education and financial technology company founded by Luis Hernán Silva. The company provides Spanish-language educational content on options trading and operates a suite of fintech platforms serving Hispanic retail investors globally. [1][2]

Company History

Opción Sigma began in 2015 as a YouTube channel created by Luis Hernán Silva Sinning to make options trading accessible to Spanish-speaking retail investors. Sigma Option LLC was formally incorporated in Maryland in 2019 and re-registered in Florida in 2021.[1][2]

Core Educational Platform

The company’s flagship platform, Opción Sigma, offers a comprehensive suite of educational resources:

YouTube channel (@OpcionSigma): Approximately 500,000 subscribers as of 2025, making it the largest Spanish-language options education channel. [3]

Course catalog: Includes Options 101, Options 202, Sigma Pro, Pro 303, Options 4 Everyone, Sigma Trader, SigmaPX (0DTE/1DTE index options), and strategy seminars (Iron Condor, Put Credit Spread, Poor Man’s Covered Call).

Sigma Club: Premium membership community offering weekly investment and speculative alerts, live trading sessions, Sunday planning sessions, a digital library of over 200 lessons, AI-powered bots, Dark Pools data, Golden Sweeps, Gamma Exposure levels, Unusual Options Activity, Max Pain (QuantData), and Market Net Flow (Tradytics).

Sigma News: Daily newsletter at 6:00 a.m. EST covering market summaries, earnings, and economic calendars.

El Café de la Mañana: Daily WhatsApp educational series focused on trading psychology and market behavior.

Sigma Live: Periodic live sessions featuring real-time market analysis.

Mobile app: Available for iOS and Android under the developer name Sigma Option LLC. [1][2]

Events

In 2023, Sigma Option hosted the first edition of the Sigma Summit in Orlando, Florida, featuring educators and options traders such as Lex Luthringhausen, Mike Butler, and Tammy Chambless. The event was attended by over 500 participants.

In 2024, Sigma Option hosted the second edition of the Sigma Summit in Orlando, Florida, sponsored by CBOE Global Markets and Tradier Brokerage. The event featured speakers including Lex Luthringhausen, Tom Sosnoff (founder of thinkorswim, tastytrade, and tastylive), Kirk Du Plessis (Option Alpha), Markus Heitkoetter, and Pablo Gil, and attracted over 1,000 attendees.

Subsidiary Platforms and Products

Opción Sigma / Sigma Option LLC operates several proprietary platforms designed to provide education, trading, and analytics for Spanish-speaking investors:

Opción Sigma (opcionsigma.com) – The company’s core educational brand offering courses such as Options 101, Options 202, Sigma Pro, Pro 303, Options 4 Everyone, Sigma Trader, and SigmaPX. Features include a digital library with over 200 lessons, Sigma Club (a premium community with trading alerts), El Café de la Mañana (daily WhatsApp educational series), Sigma News (daily newsletter), and Sigma Live (live trading sessions). Available on iOS and Android.

Sigma Trade (sigma.trade) – A Spanish-language brokerage platform integrated with Tradier Brokerage (SEC/FINRA/SIPC). Offers zero-commission trading in stocks, ETFs, and SPX index options at $0.35 per contract. Accessible via web, desktop (Trade Hawk), and mobile apps. Charts powered by TradingView. Subscription: USD $10/month. Available in 17+ Latin American countries, Spain, and the U.S.

Sigma Terminal (sigmaterminal.app) – A SaaS analytics ecosystem with two modules: Sigma Charts for advanced technical analysis and Sigma Fundamentals for fundamental company analysis. Operates on a subscription model with Memberstack authentication and Stripe payment integration.

Optionar (optionar.com) – A comprehensive options analytics platform providing over 100 pre-built strategies, Strategy Builder, live options flow, Greeks exposure analytics (GEX, DEX, VEX), institutional trading data (10+ years), congressional and insider trades monitoring, stock and ETF screeners, earnings/dividends calendar, paper trading simulator, and custom alerts. Subscription plans start at USD $16.66/month.

Greeks Insight (greeksinsight.com) – Real-time monitoring tool for options Greeks (Delta, Gamma, Theta, Vega), designed to help traders manage risk and optimize trading strategies. [1][2]

Social Media and Institutional Presence

Opción Sigma maintains an active and influential presence across social media platforms, reaching a broad Spanish-speaking audience interested in options trading and financial education:

YouTube (@OpcionSigma) – Largest Spanish-language options trading education channel in 2025, with over 500,000 subscribers. Features include educational videos, trading tutorials, market analysis, and strategy guides.

Founder Recognition – The company is directly associated with its founder, Luis Hernán Silva, a recognized figure in Latin American financial education. A separate Wikipedia article for Silva is being submitted simultaneously.

Institutional Association – Opción Sigma is affiliated with Cboe Global Markets, the world’s largest derivatives exchange, which appointed Silva as Adjunct Professor of its Options Institute in 2022. This appointment highlights the company’s credibility and notability in the financial education space. [4]

Brokerage Integration – Opción Sigma’s Sigma Trade platform is integrated with Tradier Brokerage, LLC, a U.S. broker-dealer regulated by the SEC, FINRA, and SIPC, providing institutional-level access to retail investors. [1][2]

title: Luis Silva Sinning
content:
Luis Hernan Silva Sinning (born March 13, 1980, in Mompox, Bolívar, Colombia) is a Colombian-American derivatives trader, financial educator, and entrepreneur. He is the founder of Opción Sigma, a Spanish-language financial education platform focused on options trading, and Sigma Trade, a trading platform designed for Spanish-speaking investors.

In 2022, Silva Sinning was appointed Adjunct Professor at the Options Institute of Cboe Global Markets, an educational division of one of the largest derivatives exchanges globally. [1][2][3][4]

Early life and education

Silva Sinning was born in Mompox, Bolívar, Colombia, and raised in Bogotá as the eldest of four siblings. He is the son of Hernan Silva Meñaca and Gloria Sinning Soto.

He studied Business Administration at the National University of Colombia and later earned a master’s degree in business administration from the same institution.

During his academic years, he developed an interest in financial markets, risk management, and derivatives, which would later define his professional career.[5][6][11]

Career

Early career

Before entering financial markets, Silva Sinning worked in the automotive and commercial sectors across Latin America. He held roles in financial project management at companies such as DERCO, overseeing operations across Colombia, Chile, Peru, and Bolivia.

He also served as a university lecturer in international marketing at Universidad Santo Tomás in Colombia.[8][9]

 Transition to financial markets

Silva Sinning began focusing on financial markets in the early 2010s, specializing in derivatives and options trading. His work emphasizes probability-based strategies, volatility analysis, and risk management through the use of options Greeks.

He has over a decade of experience in the securities industry and has previously taught financial derivatives and marketing at academic institutions.

Business ventures

Opción Sigma

In 2019, Silva Sinning founded Opción Sigma, a financial education platform aimed at Spanish-speaking investors. The platform offers structured courses, live trading sessions, and digital content focused on derivatives and U.S. financial markets.

The initiative was created to address the lack of accessible financial education in Spanish and has grown into a global digital education platform.

Sigma Trade

He is also the founder of Sigma Trade, a trading platform developed in partnership with Tradier Brokerage, designed to provide Spanish-language access to U.S. financial markets and trading tools.

Media and public presence

Silva Sinning produces financial education content in Spanish across multiple formats, including:

  1. Daily market briefings

  3. Live trading sessions and analysis
  4. Featured at CBOE Global Digest

  9. Revista Poder — "Luis Silva Revolutionizes Financial Education on YouTube".
  10. El Pais (Cali) — "From Colombia to Wall Street: the story of Luis Silva".
  11. Diario Occidente — "A Colombian conquers Wall Street".
  12. Revista Codigo Click — Featured editorial profile.
  13. RCN Radio — Live interview, June 14, 2025.

He maintains a presence on YouTube, where his channel focuses on explaining financial markets and options trading to Spanish-speaking audiences. [8][10]

Speaking and conferences

He has participated as a speaker and panelist in financial industry events, including:

 

  1. Options Industry Council (OIC) sessions
  2. Rankia Markets Experience (Latin America)
  3. Events organized by Tradier, Tastytrade, and NUAM Markets

Academic and institutional affiliation

title: Robert McCloud

title: Jordan Brunson

Early Life and Education

Jordan Brunson was born and raised in Dallas, Texas. He pursued his undergraduate education at Morehouse College in Atlanta, Georgia. He later earned his Doctor of Dental Surgery (DDS) degree from the University of Michigan School of Dentistry.

 

Military Service

Prior to entering private dental practice, Brunson served in the United States Army for approximately three years. During his service, he was stationed at Fort Benning, Georgia, achieved the rank of captain, and was awarded the Army Commendation Medal.

 

Career

Palmetto Family Dental

Brunson is the owner of Palmetto Family Dental, a family-owned dental practice providing general, cosmetic, and restorative dentistry services across multiple locations in Georgia.

He acquired the practice in 2011, purchasing it from a long-standing local dentist, and has since expanded operations to additional locations including Zebulon, McDonough, and Fayetteville.

Under his leadership, the practice emphasizes patient-centered care, combining modern dental techniques with a family-oriented approach to treatment.

 

Palmetto Sleep and Dental Sleep Medicine

Brunson is also affiliated with Palmetto Sleep, where he specializes in the treatment of sleep apnea and related conditions. He has personal experience with sleep apnea, which has influenced his focus on patient education and treatment in this field.

He is a certified member of the American Academy of Dental Sleep Medicine (AADSM) and provides care for conditions such as snoring, insomnia, fatigue, and other sleep-related disorders.

 

Professional Development and Memberships

Brunson has completed continuing education in multiple dental disciplines, including:

  • Pathology
  • Cosmetic dentistry
  • Periodontics
  • Prosthodontics
  • Sleep apnea treatment 

He is affiliated with several professional organizations, including:

  • American Dental Association
  • Georgia Dental Association
  • Academy of General Dentistry
  • American Academy of Facial Esthetics
  • Kappa Alpha Psi 

In addition to clinical practice, he has been involved in lecturing and sharing knowledge with dental students and peers.

 

Personal Life

Brunson resides in Georgia. He is married to Lisa Brunson, and the couple has two daughters.

Outside of his professional activities, he is involved in education and community-focused dental care initiatives.

 

Practice Philosophy

Brunson’s approach to dentistry emphasizes:

  • Patient-centered care
  • Family-oriented service
  • Accessibility across multiple communities
  • Integration of modern dental techniques

His stated vision for his practice is to create a welcoming environment where patients feel like part of a family rather than traditional clinical settings.

title: Genghis Kahn
content:
Kahn’s work spans independent music production, artist development, and digital media strategy, with a focus on building self-sustained creative platforms outside of traditional major-label systems. His approach reflects the evolving landscape of the music industry, where independent creators increasingly utilize digital tools to produce, distribute, and monetize content globally.

Early life and education

Genghis Kahn was born and raised in Brooklyn, New York, a borough widely recognized as one of the cultural centers of hip hop and urban music. Growing up in an environment shaped by diverse musical influences, street culture, and independent artistry, he developed an early interest in sound production, rhythm composition, and media creation.

His exposure to the independent music scene in New York played a formative role in shaping his creative direction, particularly in understanding the intersection between music, identity, and entrepreneurship.

Kahn later attended Full Sail University, where he pursued studies in Communications and Media Studies as well as Music Audio Production. During his time there, he gained formal training in recording techniques, sound engineering, digital production software, and media theory. His academic background provided both the technical skills and conceptual framework necessary to operate within the modern music production landscape.

Career

Music production and independent work

Kahn began his professional career as an independent music producer, initially releasing content through online platforms such as SoundCloud and other digital streaming services. Working under the alias Ivy League Fatso, he developed a catalog of music that reflects contemporary hip hop production styles, blending traditional urban influences with modern digital sound design.

His early work focused on collaborations with emerging and independent artists, positioning himself within a network of creators operating outside of mainstream industry channels. This collaborative approach allowed him to build a grassroots presence while refining his production style and expanding his creative reach.

Over time, his work evolved to incorporate broader elements of music branding, artist positioning, and digital identity. His productions often emphasize rhythm-driven compositions, layered instrumentation, and a stylistic approach aligned with independent hip hop and underground music movements.

Digital distribution and platform strategy

A defining aspect of Kahn’s career has been his focus on digital-first distribution. Rather than relying on traditional record label structures, he has utilized streaming platforms, social media, and direct-to-audience channels to release and promote music.

This strategy reflects a broader shift within the music industry toward decentralization, where artists and producers maintain greater control over their content, revenue streams, and audience engagement. Kahn’s work in this space positions him among a generation of independent creators leveraging technology to bypass conventional gatekeeping systems.

Ivy League Empire (I.L.E)

Kahn is the founder and CEO of Ivy League Empire (I.L.E), an independent music and multimedia company established as a platform for creative production and artist development.

Under his leadership, Ivy League Empire has expanded beyond music production into a multi-faceted operation that includes:

  • Music recording and production
  • Digital distribution and publishing
  • Brand development for independent artists
  • Merchandise design and printing
  • Content creation and digital marketing

The company operates with a vertically integrated model, allowing for control over multiple aspects of the creative and commercial process. This structure enables independent artists to develop and distribute their work while maintaining ownership and creative autonomy.

Entrepreneurial activities

In addition to music production, Kahn has pursued entrepreneurial ventures centered around branding and merchandise. Through Ivy League Empire, he has developed apparel and printed merchandise tied to artist identity and music releases, reflecting a broader trend of integrating fashion and music branding.

His business approach emphasizes:

  • Independent ownership
  • Scalable digital distribution
  • Direct audience engagement
  • Cross-platform brand building

This model aligns with contemporary practices in the music industry, where artists and producers often operate as multi-disciplinary entrepreneurs.

Artistic style and influences

Kahn’s production style is rooted in hip hop, with influences drawn from both traditional New York sounds and modern digital production techniques. His work often incorporates:

  • Layered beats and rhythmic structures
  • Digital sampling and synthesized elements
  • Minimalist yet atmospheric sound design
  • Collaborative vocal arrangements

His approach reflects the blending of analog-inspired production with digital innovation, characteristic of independent producers working in the 21st century.

Personal life

Genghis Kahn is married to Sheema Battle. He continues to be based in Brooklyn, New York, where he oversees his business operations and creative projects.

Legacy and significance

Kahn represents a segment of the modern music industry defined by independent production, digital entrepreneurship, and self-managed creative ecosystems. Through his work with Ivy League Empire, he has contributed to the ongoing shift toward decentralized music distribution and artist-led business models.

His career reflects broader changes in how music is produced, marketed, and consumed, particularly within independent and digital-first environments.

title: James Ault
content:
James Ault built his career in documentary filmmaking with a focus on intellectual, scientific, and human-centered narratives. His work is characterized by an interest in translating complex academic and scientific ideas into accessible visual storytelling.

He is best known for his involvement in the documentary N Is a Number: A Portrait of Paul Erdős, which explores the life and work of the Hungarian mathematician Paul Erdős.[1] The film presents Erdős not only as a mathematical figure of global significance but also as a deeply unconventional personality whose life was defined by collaboration, travel, and intellectual curiosity. Through interviews, archival material, and observational footage, the documentary constructs a layered portrait that connects abstract mathematical achievement with human experience.

The film has been widely used in academic and educational contexts, particularly within mathematics departments and institutions focused on science communication. It has been screened in universities, educational programs, and documentary film circuits where the emphasis is on bridging academic knowledge with public understanding.[2]

Ault’s work has been associated with Documentary Educational Resources, a globally recognized distributor of documentary and ethnographic films. Through this platform, his projects have been made accessible to educational institutions, libraries, and cultural organizations, extending their reach beyond traditional film audiences.[3]

Beyond his work on N Is a Number, Ault has contributed to documentary production and authorship in areas aligned with education, science, and cultural storytelling. His broader body of work reflects a consistent interest in documenting individuals and ideas that operate at the intersection of knowledge, creativity, and human experience.[4]

Selected filmography

  • N Is a Number: A Portrait of Paul Erdős (Documentary)[1]
  • Additional documentary and educational film contributions (various projects across educational distribution networks)[3][4]

Style and thematic focus

Ault’s filmmaking is defined by an emphasis on intellectual accessibility and narrative clarity. His work often focuses on individuals whose contributions lie in highly specialized fields, with a particular focus on mathematics and science.

Key characteristics of his style include:

  • A biographical approach to complex academic figures
  • Emphasis on human personality behind intellectual achievement
  • Use of interviews and archival material to ground abstract ideas in lived experience
  • A narrative structure aimed at both academic and general audiences

This approach has made his work particularly suitable for educational distribution, where films are used as teaching tools as well as cultural documentation.[2]

Distribution and academic use

Through Documentary Educational Resources, Ault’s work has been distributed internationally to universities, libraries, and educational institutions. His films are frequently included in academic curricula, particularly in courses related to mathematics, science communication, and documentary studies.[3]

The continued academic use of his work highlights its relevance beyond entertainment, positioning it within the broader field of educational media and intellectual documentary filmmaking.

Recognition and impact

Ault’s contribution to documentary cinema is primarily recognized through the educational adoption of his work rather than commercial distribution. N Is a Number: A Portrait of Paul Erdős has been noted for its ability to make abstract mathematical concepts accessible to non-specialist audiences while preserving intellectual depth.

His work has contributed to the broader genre of science and mathematics documentary filmmaking, a field that seeks to bridge the gap between academic research and public understanding.[2][4]

title: Bird Food For Life
content:

Bird Food For Life (BFFL) is a literary and lifestyle concept centered around short-form inspirational storytelling, personal reflection, and holistic well-being. Developed by author Larry Ray Plant, the concept combines elements of motivational writing, philosophy, and lifestyle guidance, emphasizing themes of health, hope, and human connection.

Overview

Bird Food For Life originated as a conceptual framework built around the idea of “feeding life” through positive inputs, including thoughts, actions, relationships, and lifestyle choices. It presents life as a series of choices that influence overall well-being, encouraging individuals to consciously engage with their environment and personal habits.

The platform combines narrative storytelling with philosophical reflections, often delivered through short, accessible texts intended to inspire readers toward a more mindful and balanced life.

Concept and philosophy

At its core, Bird Food For Life is based on the metaphor of “feeding” one’s life in the same way one nourishes the body. The concept suggests that individuals should intentionally select what they consume—both physically and mentally—from the broader “smorgasbord” of life experiences.

The philosophy emphasizes:

  • Personal choice and responsibility
  • Mindful living and awareness
  • Emotional and social connection
  • Simplicity and gratitude
  • Incremental growth (“one step at a time”)

The framework promotes the idea that small, consistent choices can lead to a more meaningful and fulfilling life experience.

Development

The concept of Bird Food For Life was developed by Larry Ray Plant following personal observations and experiences in and around Lake Havasu City, Arizona.

Initially conceived as a dietary and lifestyle reflection, the idea evolved into a broader narrative format consisting of short stories and philosophical insights. Over time, it expanded into a structured body of work aimed at sharing perspective-driven life lessons.

Publication

The primary expression of the concept is the book Bird Food For Life, which compiles a series of short, reflective stories intended to inspire readers. The work focuses on themes such as:

  • Health and healing
  • Hope and optimism
  • Humor and emotional resilience
  • Harmony and human connection 

The book has been made available through online retail platforms, including Amazon.

Themes

Recurring themes within Bird Food For Life include:

  • Holistic well-being: Integration of physical, mental, and emotional health
  • Human connection: Emphasis on relationships and shared experiences
  • Positive perspective: Encouraging optimism and resilience
  • Simplicity: Viewing life as fundamentally simple despite external complexities
  • Storytelling: Using narratives as a tool for reflection and learning

The work often frames life as a shared experience, where storytelling becomes a means of mutual growth and understanding.

Structure and format

Bird Food For Life is primarily structured as a collection of short-form narratives. These stories are designed to be concise and accessible, allowing readers to engage with individual ideas without requiring extended reading sessions.

The format reflects the broader philosophy of incremental engagement—encouraging readers to absorb insights gradually rather than through a single comprehensive narrative.

Author

Larry Ray Plant is the creator, author, and primary voice behind Bird Food For Life. He describes himself as the “originator” and “initial believer” of the concept, drawing on personal life experiences and interactions to shape the work.

His approach is rooted in experiential learning and observation, with an emphasis on human interaction and shared understanding.

Reception and positioning

Bird Food For Life is positioned within the broader category of inspirational and self-development literature. Its emphasis on short, reflective storytelling aligns it with contemporary trends in accessible motivational content.

Unlike traditional self-help frameworks that focus on structured systems or methodologies, Bird Food For Life adopts a more narrative-driven approach, relying on metaphor and personal reflection rather than prescriptive guidance.

title: Dr. Yilin Sun
content:
Yilin Sun earned her Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in Applied Linguistics and Curriculum & Instruction from the Ontario Institute for Studies in Education (OISE) at the University of Toronto, Canada. Her academic training focused on language pedagogy, curriculum development, and teacher education, areas that would later define her professional career.

Academic Career

Sun has been affiliated with the Seattle Colleges District for over 25 years, where she has held multiple academic and administrative roles. As a tenured professor, her teaching has centered on English language instruction for non-native speakers, TESOL teacher training, and curriculum design.

In her capacity as Director of Faculty Development, Sun has led initiatives aimed at improving teaching effectiveness, supporting faculty across disciplines, and promoting inclusive, culturally responsive education. Her work has involved collaboration with faculty, staff, and students from diverse linguistic and cultural backgrounds.

Her teaching and administrative contributions have been particularly focused on:

  • English language instruction (ESOL)
  • TESOL teacher training
  • Assessment and curriculum development
  • Faculty professional development
  • International education initiatives

Leadership in TESOL

Sun served as President of the TESOL International Association from 2014 to 2015. Her presidency marked a significant milestone, as she became the first bilingual Chinese–English speaking Asian woman to lead the organization in its 50-year history.

During her tenure, she emphasized global collaboration, teacher development, and expanding access to English language education. Her leadership contributed to strengthening international partnerships and advancing professional standards in TESOL.

Fulbright Scholarship

Sun was awarded a Fulbright Senior Scholar grant through the Fulbright Program for the 2011–2012 academic year. As a Fulbright Scholar, she engaged in international academic exchange, contributing to the development of English language teaching capacity and cross-cultural understanding.

Awards and Recognition

In 2021, Sun received the English Language Programs 30@30 Achievement Award from the U.S. Department of State. The award recognized her as one of thirty English Language Specialists who have made a lasting impact on the program and the TESOL field since 1991.

The recognition highlighted her contributions to:

  • Building English teaching capacity globally
  • Supporting international education initiatives
  • Promoting mutual understanding through language education

Her achievements were also covered by West Seattle Blog, which reported on her recognition for excellence in English teaching.

Publications and Scholarly Work

Sun is an author and co-author of numerous academic works, including:

  • Books on TESOL and language education
  • Book chapters in edited academic volumes
  • Peer-reviewed journal articles

Her research and publications focus on language pedagogy, teacher education, and curriculum innovation. In addition to her written work, she has delivered plenary and featured presentations at national and international conferences, contributing to professional discourse in applied linguistics and TESOL.

Professional Contributions

Beyond her institutional and leadership roles, Sun has contributed extensively to the global TESOL community through:

  • International teacher training programs
  • Conference keynote and plenary speaking
  • Curriculum development initiatives
  • Cross-cultural education projects

Her work has been particularly influential in advancing English language education in international contexts and supporting educators worldwide.

Legacy and Impact

Yilin Sun is regarded as a significant figure in TESOL, particularly for her leadership, advocacy for multilingual educators, and contributions to global English language education. Her career reflects a sustained commitment to improving teaching quality, expanding educational access, and fostering intercultural understanding.

title: Raquel Durden
content:
Raquel Durden is an American author, holistic wellness advocate, and retired United States Army lieutenant colonel. She is best known for her book Dial Down: Holistic Strategies to Move from Chaos to Calm (2025), a guide that combines personal experience with practical wellness techniques designed for veterans, first responders, and individuals navigating high-stress environments.

Durden is the co-founder and chairperson of Humble Warrior Wellness & Yoga, a nonprofit organization that supports women veterans and first responders through community engagement, wellness education, and holistic practices. In recognition of her leadership and advocacy, she was named Georgia Woman Veteran of the Year in 2025.

Early Life and Education

Raquel Durden was born in Two Rivers, Wisconsin, and raised in nearby Manitowoc. She developed an early connection to nature through activities such as hiking, fishing, and camping. These formative experiences later influenced her emphasis on grounding, resilience, and connection within her wellness philosophy.

At the age of 17, Durden enlisted in the United States Army, motivated by a desire for service and personal growth. Following her military career, she pursued higher education, earning a Master of Business Administration from the State University of New York at Oswego and attending the University of Wisconsin–Stevens Point.

Military Career

Durden served in the United States Army for 25 years, retiring with the rank of lieutenant colonel. Her military career included roles as a paratrooper, combat veteran, and military intelligence analyst.

She deployed with the 10th Mountain Division during Operation Restore Hope in Somalia in 1993, contributing to humanitarian and stabilization efforts. Her service also included assignments in Egypt and South Korea.

Throughout her career, Durden held leadership roles ranging from company-level command to battalion command. Prior to retirement in 2012, she commanded the Georgia Army National Guard’s 221st Military Intelligence Battalion, overseeing personnel, operations, and intelligence coordination.

Holistic Wellness and Writing

Following her retirement from military service, Durden transitioned into holistic wellness, drawing from her personal experiences with stress, trauma, and recovery.

In 2025, she published Dial Down: Holistic Strategies to Move from Chaos to Calm, which presents a combination of research-informed wellness techniques and lived experience. The book is aimed particularly at veterans and high-stress professionals, offering approaches to emotional regulation, resilience, and balance.

Her work emphasizes breathwork, mindfulness, physical movement such as yoga, and the importance of community support. Her wellness philosophy is also informed by her personal journey, including her experience as a cancer survivor and yoga practitioner.

Durden has participated in author showcases and literary discussions, and her work has been featured in wellness-focused and author-centered media platforms.

Humble Warrior Wellness & Yoga

In 2018, Durden co-founded Humble Warrior Wellness & Yoga, a nonprofit organization dedicated to supporting women veterans and first responders.

The organization focuses on reducing isolation and fostering connection through wellness-based programming. It offers retreats, workshops, and community engagement initiatives that integrate yoga, mindfulness, breathwork, and peer support.

The nonprofit also maintains an active digital presence, including video-based programming and online content designed to expand its reach beyond local communities and provide accessible wellness resources nationally.

Media, Speaking, and Public Engagement

Durden has participated in a range of speaking engagements, literary events, and wellness-focused programs across the United States.

She has spoken at national platforms, including the Military Influencer Conference in 2025, where she addressed topics related to veteran wellness, resilience, and life transition after military service.

Her work has been featured in media outlets and regional broadcasts, including television coverage highlighting her contributions to mental health awareness and veteran advocacy. She has also been featured in She Served magazine.

In addition, Durden has participated in author showcases, interviews, and community-based discussions related to her book and advocacy work.

Recognition

In November 2025, Durden was named Georgia Woman Veteran of the Year in recognition of her contributions to veteran advocacy, wellness education, and community leadership.

She has also been recognized through various speaking and community platforms for her continued work supporting veterans and promoting holistic mental health practices.

Personal Life

Durden resides in Bogart, Georgia, with her husband, Dave Durden, a fellow combat veteran. The couple share interests in travel, motorcycle riding, scuba diving, and animal welfare.

title: James C. Aronson
content:
James C. Aronson (born August 3, 1953) is an American restoration ecologist, author, and scientific editor. He is a Senior Scientist Emeritus at the Missouri Botanical Garden's Center for Conservation and Sustainable Development, and co-founder and president of the Ecological Health Network, an international initiative working at the intersection of ecological restoration and public health.

Aronson is among the most widely cited researchers in restoration ecology, with over 40,000 citations recorded on Google Scholar and an h-index of 82 as of 2025. He has authored or co-authored more than 225 peer-reviewed publications and 10 books, including several standard texts in the field. His work has helped establish the conceptual vocabulary, analytical frameworks, and international standards for ecological restoration, and has extended the discipline into ecological economics, environmental policy, and public health.

Early life and education

James C. Aronson was born on August 3, 1953, in St. Louis, Missouri. He began his university studies at Columbia University in New York (1971–1973), concentrating on cultural anthropology and languages. He later transferred to the University of California, Davis, studying botany and palaeobotany, before completing a Bachelor of Science in biology at Washington University in St. Louis in 1978, where he worked part-time in the herbarium at the Missouri Botanical Garden under the direction of Peter H. Raven.

During a period between his undergraduate studies and doctoral work, Aronson spent time in Israel, living and working on two kibbutzim and apprenticing with John Maurice at Kibbutz Hazorea, a master nurseryman and inventor of micropropagation techniques for subtropical fruit and nut trees.

Following his undergraduate degree, Aronson traveled to Peru to spend approximately twenty months (1977–1979) collecting botanical specimens in the Peruvian Amazon as a field co-coordinator for the Flora of Peru project at the Missouri Botanical Garden, working alongside botanist Alwyn Gentry. This experience deepened his interest in economic botany, agroforestry, and the management of degraded landscapes.

From 1980 to 1987, Aronson served as Plant Introduction Officer at the Boyko Institute in Beer-Sheva, Israel, evaluating wild and cultivated plants from arid and semi-arid regions worldwide for drought and salinity tolerance, and maintaining experimental nurseries and a seed bank. He also served briefly as Interim Director of the Desert Run-off Farms Unit at Sde Boker (1985–1986).

Aronson completed his Doctor of Philosophy in plant ecology and biogeography at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 1990. In 2002, he obtained a Habilitation à Diriger des Recherches (HDR) from the University of Toulouse, the French qualification authorising the supervision of doctoral research.

Career

Centre national de la recherche scientifique (1992–2016)

In 1992, Aronson was recruited by the Centre national de la recherche scientifique (CNRS) as a researcher in restoration ecology at the Centre d'Écologie Fonctionnelle et Évolutive (CEFE) in Montpellier, France — among the first such appointments in that discipline in France. He remained there until 2016, co-founding and directing the Restoration Ecology Group and undertaking research on ecosystem degradation, rehabilitation, and restoration across Mediterranean-climate regions, arid zones, and tropical forests. During this period he also maintained long-standing collaborations in Chile, South Africa, Brazil, and Madagascar.

Missouri Botanical Garden (2009–present)

Aronson joined the Missouri Botanical Garden as a Senior Scientist at its Center for Conservation and Sustainable Development, a position he holds as Senior Scientist Emeritus. In this role he has contributed to conservation and restoration programs in Madagascar and other biodiversity-rich regions, integrating field botany with ecological restoration science.

Ecological Health Network (2013–present)

In 2013, Aronson co-founded the Restoring Natural Capital Alliance, which was subsequently reorganised as the Ecological Health Network (EHN), a non-governmental initiative. As co-founder, president, and interim director, he has led the network's work at the intersection of biocultural restoration, ecosystem health, and human wellbeing, collaborating with health scientists, conservation practitioners, and Indigenous knowledge-holders globally.

Research and contributions

Aronson's research spans restoration ecology, dryland botany, Mediterranean-climate ecosystems, tropical forests, marine ecosystem restoration, and the links between ecosystem health and human health. His early work focused on halophyte ecology and the identification of salt-tolerant plants for use in arid-land agriculture, resulting in the 1989 reference volume HALOPH: Salt Tolerant Plants of the World (University of Arizona Press), from which the interactive online database eHALOPH was subsequently developed.

From 1993 onward, Aronson and his collaborators published foundational papers on the vocabulary and conceptual framework of ecological restoration, distinguishing restoration, rehabilitation, and reclamation, and establishing the importance of the "ecosystem of reference" in guiding restoration targets. His 2007 book Ecological Restoration: Principles, Values, and Structure of an Emerging Profession (Island Press, with André Clewell), updated in a second edition in 2013, became a standard text in the field.

A central thread of his work has been the concept of "natural capital" — the stock of natural resources and ecosystem services that underpin human wellbeing — and its application to the economics and policy of ecological restoration. He edited the 2007 volume Restoring Natural Capital: Science, Business, and Practice (Island Press) and contributed to the Economics of Ecosystems and Biodiversity (TEEB) initiative of the G8, UNEP, and the European Commission (2009–2013).

Aronson has been a leading critic of the "novel ecosystems" concept as applied to conservation and restoration policy, arguing that it risks providing justification for abandoning restoration goals in degraded landscapes. He has also contributed to the development of international restoration standards, co-authoring all three editions of the Society for Ecological Restoration's International Principles and Standards for the Practice of Ecological Restoration (2019, and 3rd ed. in press 2026).

More recently, his research and advocacy have focused on the relationship between ecological restoration and human health outcomes, through the journal Environmental Conservation and the Ecological Health Network's work on synergistic restoration of ecosystems and human health.

Editorial roles and book series

From 2002 to 2020, Aronson served as Editor-in-Chief of the Society for Ecological Restoration / Island Press book series Science and Practice of Ecological Restoration, overseeing the publication of 27 volumes. He has been a member of the editorial board of Restoration Ecology since 1992, of BioScience since 2015, and of Environmental Conservation since 2024. He has served as guest editor for special issues in Ecology & Society, Frontiers in Ecology and Evolution, Ecological Restoration, and the Annals of the Missouri Botanical Garden, among others.

title: Jess Caleb Bhuiyan Yliniemi
content:
He is the founder of usa.healthcare, a healthcare awareness initiative focused on promoting wellness campaigns, healthcare branding, and public health messaging through digital platforms and consumer-focused branding strategies. He has also been associated with multiple ventures and organizations including PINKYFINN LLC, Orkazoo LTD, astronaut.health, and other healthcare-related initiatives.

Early life and education

Jess Caleb Bhuiyan Yliniemi studied international business and business administration. He attended Haaga-Helia University of Applied Sciences and later pursued MBA studies at the University of Phoenix. His academic background contributed to his work in entrepreneurship, international branding, and healthcare innovation.

Career
Engineering and project management

During the early stages of his professional career, Yliniemi worked in engineering and project management positions. He worked as a project engineer at Balfour Beatty US and later served in project management roles associated with Ecocat Oy in Finland. His experience in infrastructure, engineering operations, and strategic planning later influenced his entrepreneurial and healthcare ventures.

Healthcare and entrepreneurship

In 2021, Yliniemi launched usa.healthcare, a healthcare-oriented initiative aimed at improving healthcare awareness, accessibility, and digital healthcare communication. The platform gained visibility for integrating healthcare messaging with apparel branding, digital campaigns, and wellness-oriented public initiatives.

The initiative focused on healthcare advocacy campaigns, wellness awareness, vaccination awareness branding, and international healthcare communication projects. Through these initiatives, Yliniemi became associated with healthcare branding strategies that merged emotional storytelling with consumer engagement.

He additionally founded PINKYFINN LLC, a Hawaii-based company involved in branding and healthcare-related business operations. Over time, he expanded his involvement into additional projects including Health Innovation Village, CarpeDiem Health LLC, Gaza.Health, Dhaka.Healthcare, and astronaut.health.

 

Public service and advisory work

Yliniemi has also participated in healthcare advocacy and emergency response initiatives. He has been associated with FEMA-related reservist activities and nonprofit healthcare initiatives connected to mentorship, emergency preparedness, and humanitarian awareness.

In addition to his entrepreneurial work, he has participated in volunteer and nonprofit initiatives associated with healthcare awareness, wellness advocacy, and international humanitarian communication campaigns.

Business ventures

USA Healthcare

USA Healthcare is a healthcare awareness and branding initiative founded by Yliniemi in Honolulu, Hawaii. The platform promotes healthcare communication, wellness campaigns, public health awareness, and healthcare-focused branding projects through digital media, merchandise, and public engagement campaigns.

The initiative became known for combining healthcare awareness with branding and emotional storytelling designed to increase public engagement with wellness and healthcare initiatives.

Orkazoo LTD

Yliniemi has also been associated with Orkazoo LTD, where he has served in leadership and strategic development capacities. His work with the organization has focused on branding, business strategy, and innovation-oriented projects.

title: Jacob Eapen
content:
Jacob Eapen is an Indian-American pediatrician and public health physician based in Fremont, California. He has served as a medical director within Alameda Health System and has been elected multiple times to the board of the Washington Hospital Healthcare System. In 2007, he received the Ellis Island Medal of Honor. [1][2]

Early life and education

Eapen was born in Thiruvananthapuram, India. He earned a medical degree from Government Medical College, Thiruvananthapuram, in 1976 and completed postgraduate training in pediatrics at Christian Medical College, Ludhiana. [3]

He later moved to the United States and earned a Master of Public Health degree from the University of California, Berkeley. He subsequently completed pediatric residency training at Stanford University School of Medicine. [4]

Career

Before moving to the United States, Eapen worked as a consultant pediatrician at Aga Khan Foundation Hospital in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. He later served on the pediatric faculty at the University of Sokoto in Nigeria. [2]

In 1988, he worked with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in the Philippines, where he participated in healthcare services for refugees. [3]

Eapen later joined Alameda County Health Services in California as a pediatrician and public health physician. In 1999, he was appointed Public Health Commissioner for Alameda County. [2]

He subsequently served as medical director within Alameda Health System, one of California's public healthcare systems. [5]

In 2004, Eapen was elected to the board of directors of the Washington Hospital Healthcare System. He has since been reelected to the board on multiple occasions. [5]

Eapen has also served on healthcare and public health advisory bodies, including the advisory board of the School of Public Health at the University of California, Berkeley, and healthcare organizations in California.

Recognition and Honors

In 2007, Eapen received the Ellis Island Medal of Honor, an American award recognizing contributions to society and public service. [1][2]

He was featured in Stanford University School of Medicine's publication ''Forty Careers in Medicine'' and was recognized among the institution's distinguished alumni. [4]

Eapen has received the California Medical Board Physician Recognition Award, the Mother Teresa Award presented by Friends of the South Asian American Communities (FOSAAC), and achievement awards from several Indian-American community organizations.

He has also received Distinguished Alumni and Lifetime Achievement awards from Government Medical College, Thiruvananthapuram.

Personal life

Eapen is married to Shirley Jacob. They have two children, Naveen Jacob and Sandhya Jacob.

title: Susanne Hannestad
content:
Susanne Hannestad (born 1961) is a Norwegian entrepreneur, fintech executive, and former international handball player. She is best known as the Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Fintech Mundi, a global fintech accelerator and advisory firm headquartered in Oslo, Norway. Hannestad is a board director in several companies within sustainable banking, digital cash, and fintech, and has held senior management positions at Nordea. She is widely recognised as one of the leading voices in the Nordic fintech ecosystem and a prominent advocate for diversity and financial inclusion in the industry. FFNews

Early life and education

Hannestad was born in 1961 and is Norwegian. She is an alumna of Oslo University, INSEAD, and Northeastern University; at INSEAD and Northeastern she has also served as a lecturer. She holds an MBA from Northeastern University and a Master of Business and Marketing from Oslo Business School, and completed executive studies at INSEAD. In 2006 she participated in INSEAD's Advanced Management Programme (AMP), and in 2022 she earned a Corporate Director Certificate from Harvard Business School. She later became President of the INSEAD Alumni Association Norway. Wikipedia + 2

Handball career

Before her business career, Hannestad had a significant sporting background. She played 43 matches for the Norwegian national handball team between 1979 and 1983, and participated in the 1982 World Women's Handball Championship, where Norway placed seventh. She was part of Norway's national handball team for seven years. WikipediaZimpler

Career in financial services

Hannestad spent approximately ten years at Nordea, leaving in 2012. During her tenure she rose to several senior executive positions. She held several EVP and SVP positions at Nordea and served as a board member on the MasterCard Europe Advisory Board. At Nordea, she served as Director of Nordea Finance and Head of Cards, building up the cards business across the Nordic and Baltic regions. Through Nordea, she gained access to associated board positions including Visa Norway, MasterCard Forum, and eventually MasterCard Europe. Riga TechGirls + 3

Zwipe and entry into fintech

In 2009 — three years before leaving Nordea — Hannestad became Chair of Zwipe, a Norwegian fintech start-up, at a time when the term "fintech" had not yet entered common usage. Zwipe launched the world's first contactless fingerprint-authenticated payment card technology in 2014, and the company was subsequently listed on the Oslo Stock Exchange with global operations. She served as Executive Chairman of Zwipe until 2015. Riga TechGirlsFindexable

Founding of Fintech Mundi

While working at Zwipe, Hannestad observed the growing global volume of fintech companies and the need for structured support in scaling them. She connected with contacts in London, Tel Aviv, and Dublin, and together they discussed how their combined experience and networks could help fintech companies grow. This collaboration became the founding idea for Fintech Mundi, established in 2015. Riga TechGirls

Board and advisory roles

Hannestad has maintained an exceptionally active board career across the European fintech landscape. She has served as Chairman of Zimpler AB and VIO Media AS; Independent Director at Crunchfish AB; Director at BankBridge AS, Blippit AB, Monty UK Global Ltd., and Neonomics AS; and Non-Executive Director at Monty Mobile Ltd., ClearBank Group Holdings Ltd., and Triodos Bank NV. In former roles, she served as Chairman at Payr AS, and as a Director at Zwipe AS and NOBA Group AB. MarketScreenerMarketScreener

Her completed roles over recent years also include Chairwoman at Neonomics AS, Payr AS, and Zwipe AS, and board membership at Nordax AB and Blippit AB. Crunchfish

Advocacy for diversity and financial inclusion

Hannestad has been a prominent voice on gender diversity in the fintech industry. She has spoken about how her Nordic upbringing instilled an appreciation for collaboration, noting that the Nordic countries' small populations and intimate professional communities make network-building central to the culture. She has also been an advocate for bringing more women into the fintech sector and served as Chair of the Fintech Diversity Radar Advisory Board at Findexable. Harringtonstarr

She has served as Regional Ambassador for the Nordics and Baltics at Findexable, an organisation that produces the Global Fintech Index. Findexable

Personal life

Hannestad is based in Oslo, Norway. She founded Bozan AS, a personal holding company through which she holds shares in companies including Crunchfish AB. She is President of the INSEAD Alumni Association Norway.

title: Fintech Mundi
content:
Fintech Mundi is a global fintech accelerator and advisory firm founded in 2015 and headquartered in Oslo, Norway. The company provides fintech businesses worldwide with access to a vast network of financial services experts, enabling them to commercialise, scale, and reach global markets, and operates from multiple locations including London, Oslo, Tel Aviv, and Dublin. It is one of the best-known specialist advisors to the Nordic and Baltic fintech ecosystem, and serves as a growth advisor to the Mastercard Lighthouse programme. 

Background and founding

Fintech Mundi was founded in 2015 by Susanne Hannestad, who at the time was Executive Chairman of Zwipe, a Norwegian biometric payments company. Having observed the rapid growth of the global fintech sector, she identified a gap in the market for experienced advisors who could help fintech companies scale internationally. She connected with contacts across London, Tel Aviv, and Dublin, and together they established Fintech Mundi as a platform drawing on their combined networks and domain expertise. The name reflects the firm's global ("mundi" being Latin for "world") and cross-border orientation. 

Mission and services

Fintech Mundi helps high-potential financial technology companies to develop their ideas, commercialise their products, and grow their businesses internationally. Its stated areas of expertise include business strategy, commercialisation, business development and scaling, marketing, and communications. 

The firm positions itself as offering unparalleled expertise in global financial technologies, a proven track record for scaling and launching companies in global markets, and a unique ecosystem for global fintech growth, underpinned by a trusted industry network. 

Team and structure

Fintech Mundi's core team includes Susanne Hannestad (Partner, Oslo), Simon Hardie (Partner, London), Denise Gee (Partner, Twickenham), and Colum Rafferty (Advisor). The firm operates as a lean advisory partnership rather than a traditional venture capital fund, and does not take equity stakes in the companies it advises as part of its standard model. 

Mastercard Lighthouse partnership

One of Fintech Mundi's most prominent ongoing engagements is as a growth advisor to the Mastercard Lighthouse programmes in the Nordic and Baltic region. The Mastercard Lighthouse FINITIV programme runs over a three-month period and offers Nordic and Baltic fintech and fintech-enabler startups the opportunity to work with stakeholders such as Mastercard, tier-one Nordic banks including SEB, Danske Bank, DNB, Swedbank and OP Financial Group, technology partners such as AWS, and programme advisors including Fintech Mundi and Invenio Growth. 

Fintech Mundi has been named as a growth advisor in successive Mastercard Lighthouse cohorts, sitting alongside partners such as AWS. The Mastercard Lighthouse FINITIV programme has reached its 14th round, with Fintech Mundi continuing to feature as a named programme advisor. 

Financial Inclusion Summit and thought leadership

Hannestad has organised events such as the Financial Inclusion Summit in Oslo, held in partnership with Mastercard, to showcase Nordic fintech companies providing solutions for emerging markets in Asia, Africa, and Latin America. Fintech Mundi has also produced industry research through the Fintech Disruptors Report series in partnership with MagnaCarta. 

The firm publishes an annual Nordic Insight Briefing focusing on trends in digital financial services across the Nordic region, and has produced thought leadership on markets including Saudi Arabia and the DACH region of Europe. 

Nordic and Baltic focus

He is the founder of several entertainment-focused companies and has served as legal counsel and advisor to numerous creative professionals and organizations. Early Life and Education

Renu Bakshi is a Canadian journalist, broadcaster, communications consultant, and columnist based in British Columbia, Canada. She is known for her work as a television journalist with CTV and for her later career in strategic communications, media relations, crisis communications, and executive media training. She has also written opinion columns and commentary for a number of Canadian newspapers and digital publications. In 2024, she was recognized among the Top 500 Influential Business Leaders in British Columbia.[1]

Early life and family background

Bakshi is based in British Columbia, Canada. Her family has roots in Punjab, India. Her maternal grandfather, Hansraj Sharma, immigrated to Canada from British India in 1930, arriving in Vancouver via Hong Kong, San Francisco, and Seattle.[2]

Bakshi has written about her family's immigration history and experiences as part of the South Asian community in British Columbia. In a 2023 column discussing the legacy of colonialism and the British monarchy, she recounted the experiences of her parents and extended family, including their settlement in British Columbia's forestry communities and their contributions to Canadian society.[2]

Career

Broadcast journalism

Bakshi began her career in broadcast journalism and worked as a television news anchor and journalist with CTV. During her journalism career, she reported on news, politics, public affairs, and current events in British Columbia and elsewhere in Canada.[3]

Her work in television journalism focused on news presentation, public affairs reporting, and current affairs coverage, contributing to her profile as a media commentator and communications professional.[4]

Communications consulting

Following her journalism career, Bakshi established Renu Bakshi Communications Inc., a communications consultancy specializing in crisis communications, media relations, strategic communications, and executive media training.[5]

Through her consulting practice, she has advised corporate, government, and non-profit clients on reputation management, stakeholder engagement, crisis response, and public communications. She has also provided media training for executives and organizational leaders preparing for public appearances and media interviews.[5][6]

Writing and commentary

In addition to her communications work, Bakshi has contributed opinion columns and commentary to Canadian publications. Her writing has addressed topics including public affairs, leadership, communications, media issues, politics, immigration, multiculturalism, and the historical legacy of colonialism.[2][7]

Her articles have appeared in publications including:

  • Business in Vancouver
  • National Post
  • Vancouver Sun
  • Coast Reporter
  • North Shore News
  • Richmond News
  • Tri-City News[7]

Recognition

Bakshi was included in the Top 500 Influential Business Leaders in British Columbia, recognizing her contributions to communications, journalism, and public affairs in the province.[1]

Selected topics and public commentary

Bakshi has written extensively about immigration, multiculturalism, and the experiences of South Asian Canadians. In a 2023 opinion article published by the Coast Reporter, she examined the legacy of the British Empire through the history of her own family, reflecting on colonialism, migration, and the experiences of Indian immigrants in Canada across multiple generations.[2]

title: Rene Reid
content:
James C. Aronson (born August 3, 1953) is an American restoration ecologist, author, and scientific editor. He is a Senior Scientist Emeritus at the Missouri Botanical Garden's Center for Conservation and Sustainable Development, and co-founder and president of the Ecological Health Network, an international initiative working at the intersection of ecological restoration and public health.

Aronson is among the most widely cited researchers in restoration ecology, with over 40,000 citations recorded on Google Scholar and an h-index of 82 as of 2025. He has authored or co-authored more than 225 peer-reviewed publications and 16 books, including several standard texts in the field of ecological restoration. His work has helped clarify and strengthen the field's linkages with ecological economics, environmental conversation and policy, and human health and wellbeing.

Early life and education

James C. Aronson was born on August 3, 1953, in St. Louis, Missouri. He began his university studies at Columbia University in New York (1971–1973), concentrating on cultural anthropology and languages. He later transferred to the University of California, Davis, studying botany and palaeobotany, before completing a Bachelor of Science in biology at Washington University in St. Louis in 1978, where he worked part-time in the herbarium at the Missouri Botanical Garden under the direction of Peter H. Raven.

During a period between his undergraduate studies and doctoral work, Aronson spent time in Israel, living and working on two kibbutzim and apprenticing with John Maurice at Kibbutz Hazorea, a master nurseryman and inventor of micropropagation techniques for subtropical fruit and nut trees.

Following his undergraduate degree, Aronson traveled to Peru to spend approximately twenty months (1977–1979) collecting botanical specimens in the Peruvian Amazon as a field co-coordinator for the Flora of Peru project at the Missouri Botanical Garden, working alongside botanists Camilo Díaz, and the renowned Alwyn Gentry. This experience deepened his interest in economic botany, agroforestry, landscape ecology and history, and revitalization of degraded ecosystems and landscapes, all of which were relevant to the transdisciplinary science and practice of ecological restoration that only emerged clearly in the late 1980s.

From 1980 to 1987, Aronson served as Plant Introduction Officer at the Boyko Institute in Beer-Sheva, Israel, evaluating wild and cultivated plants from arid and semi-arid regions worldwide for drought and salinity tolerance, and maintaining experimental nurseries and a seed bank. He also served briefly as Interim Director of the Desert Run-off Farm founded at Ein Avdat by Michael Evenari (1985–1986).

Aronson completed his Doctor of Philosophy in plant ecology and biogeography at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 1990. In 2002, he obtained a Habilitation à Diriger des Recherches (HDR) from the University of Toulouse, the French qualification authorising the supervision of doctoral research.

Career

Centre national de la recherche scientifique (1992–2016)

In 1992, Aronson was recruited by the Centre national de la recherche scientifique (CNRS) as a researcher in restoration ecology at the Centre d'Écologie Fonctionnelle et Évolutive (CEFE) in Montpellier, France, among the first such appointments in that discipline in France. He remained there until 2016, co-directing the Restoration Ecology Group and undertaking research on ecosystem degradation, rehabilitation, and restoration in arid, semiarid and mediterranean-climate regions, and tropical forests. During this period he also maintained long-standing collaborations in Chile, South Africa, Brazil, and Madagascar.

Missouri Botanical Garden (2009–present)

Aronson rejoined the Missouri Botanical Garden as a Senior Scientist at its Center for Conservation and Sustainable Development, a position he holds as Senior Scientist Emeritus. In this role he has contributed to conservation, sustainability and restoration programs in Madagascar and other biodiversity-rich regions, integrating field botany and plant ecology with social-ecological restoration science and practice.

Ecological Health Network (2013–present)

In 2013, Aronson co-founded the Restoring Natural Capital Alliance, which was subsequently absorbed into the Ecological Health Network (EHN), a non-governmental initiative founded in 2017.As co-founder, president, and interim director of the EHN, he leads the organization's ongoing work with sites and hubs of sites aiming to assist restoration of ecosystem health and human health holistically, in a social-ecological and biocultural fashion.

Research and contributions

Aronson's research spans restoration ecology, dryland botany, biogeography, desert trees, mediterranean-climate ecosystems, tropical forests, marine ecosystem restoration, and the links between ecosystem health and human health. Some of his early work focused on halophyte ecology and biogeography and the identification of salt-tolerant plants for use in arid-land agriculture, resulting in the 1989 reference volume HALOPH: Salt Tolerant Plants of the World (University of Arizona Press), from which the interactive online database eHALOPH was subsequently developed.

From 1993 onward, Aronson and his collaborators published foundational papers on the vocabulary and conceptual framework of ecological restoration, distinguishing restoration, rehabilitation, and reclamation, and establishing the importance of the ecosystem of reference and ecosystem trajectories in planning, guiding, and fine-tuning desired restoration targets in light of ecosystems' responses to restorative interventions over time.

A central thread of his work has been the concept of natural capital — the stock of natural resources and ecosystem services that underpin human wellbeing — and its application to the economics and policy of ecological restoration. With ecologist Suzanne J. Dean and economist James Blignaut, he co-edited the influential 2007 volume Restoring Natural Capital: Science, Business, and Practice (Island Press) and co-authored many papers in this area in the following years, and contributed to the Economics of Ecosystems and Biodiversity (TEEB) initiative of the G8, UNEP, and the European Commission (2009–2013). From 2005 to the present, he serves as co-director of ASSET Research (Africa's Search for Sound Economic Trajectories), a platform for capacity-building and inter-disciplinary work based in South Africa and led by Prof. James Blignaut.

Aronson has been a leading critic of the novel ecosystems concept as applied to conservation and restoration policy, arguing that it risks providing justification for abandoning or diluting restoration goals in degraded landscapes. He has also contributed to the development of international restoration standards, co-authoring all three editions of the Society for Ecological Restoration's International Principles and Standards for the Practice of Ecological Restoration (2016, 2019, and 3rd ed. in press 2026).

More recently, his work has focused on the relationship between ecological restoration and human health outcomes.In the course of his career, he has had the privilege of mentoring gifted graduate students and early-career professionals from many different countries and cultures.

Editorial roles and book series

From 2002 to 2020, Aronson served as Editor-in-Chief of the Society for Ecological Restoration / Island Press book series Science and Practice of Ecological Restoration, overseeing the publication of 27 volumes. He has been a member of the editorial board of Restoration Ecology since 1992, of BioScience since 2015, and several other journals. He has served as guest editor for special issues in Ecology & Society, Frontiers in Ecology and Evolution, Ecological Restoration, Environmental Conservation and the Annals of the Missouri Botanical Garden, among others.

Selected books

Aronson, J. (1989). HALOPH: Salt Tolerant Plants of the World. University of Arizona Press.

Blondel, J., & Aronson, J. (1999). Biology and Wildlife of the Mediterranean Region. Oxford University Press.

Clewell, A. F., & Aronson, J. (2007; 2nd ed. 2013). Ecological Restoration: Principles, Values, and Structure of an Emerging Profession. Island Press.

Clewell, A. F., & Aronson, J. (2010). La Restauration Ecologique: Principes, Valeurs, et Structure d'une Profession Emergente. Actes Sud.

Blondel, J., Aronson, J., Bodiou, J.-Y., & Bœuf, G. (2010). The Mediterranean Basin: Biological Diversity in Space and Time. Oxford University Press.

Le Floc'h, E., & Aronson, J. (2013). Les Arbres des Déserts: Enjeux et promesses. Actes Sud.

L'Enfant, P., Gudefin, A., Aronson, J., et al. (2015). Restauration écologique des petits fonds côtiers de Méditerranée. CREM-IEEM Editions.

L'Enfant, P., Gudefin, A., Aronson, J., et al. (2016). Ecological Restoration of Fish Nurseries in Shallow Coastal Areas of the Mediterranean Basin. CREM-IEEM Editions.

Aronson, J., Milton, S. J., & Blignaut, J. N. (Eds.) (2007). Restoring Natural Capital: Science, Business, and Practice. Island Press.

Van Andel, J., & Aronson, J. (Eds.) (2006; 2nd ed. 2012). Restoration Ecology: The New Frontier. Wiley-Blackwell.

Aronson, J., Pereira, J. S., & Pausas, J. (Eds.) (2009). Cork Oak Woodlands on the Edge. Island Press.

Roy, J., Aronson, J., & di Castri, F. (Eds.) (1995). Time Scales in the Response to Water Stress. SPB Academic Publishers.

Pontanier, R., M'Hiri, A., Akrimi, N., Aronson, J., & Le Floc'h, E. (Eds.) (1995). L'Homme peut-il refaire ce qu'il a défait? John Libby Eurotext.

Bautista, S., Aronson, J., & Vallejo, R. (Eds.) (2010). Land Restoration to Combat Desertification. Fundación CEAM.

Aronson, J., Le Floc'h, E., & Aronson, T.B. (in prep.). Native Desert Canopies: Alternative Future for Global Drylands. Oxford University Press.

Awards and recognition

1985 — Appeared in the documentary film The Plant Hunters, directed by Peter Coulson.

2007 — Society for Ecological Restoration Award for Communications in Restoration Ecology.

2011 — A new species of Araceae, Anthurium jamesii Croat, endemic to Peru, named in recognition of his contributions to applied tropical botany and ecological restoration.

2013 — ASSET (Africa's Search for Sound Economic Trajectories) Research received the Human Capacity Building Award from the South African Water Resources Commission for Restoring Natural Capital projects, in which Aronson played a leading role.

2014 — Co-authored book Les Arbres des Déserts: Enjeux et promesses (Actes Sud, 2013) awarded the Paul Bourdarie Prize by the French Académie des Sciences d'Outre-Mer.

2015 — Appointed to the BioScience editorial board for ecological restoration.

Personal life

Aronson and Joëlle Fischer have two grown-up  children, Thibaud and Perrine, who are both avid travellers, explorers and naturalists.

Aronson's research spans restoration ecology, dryland botany, biogeography, desert trees, mediterranean-climate ecosystems, tropical forests, marine ecosystem restoration, and the links between ecosystem health and human health.
